recipes.name: Broccoli Quiche with Mashed Potato Crust

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add potatoes and cook until tender but still firm, about 15 minutes; drain. Meanwhile, place broccoli in a steamer over 1 inch of boiling water, and cover. Cook until tender but still firm, about 2 to 6 minutes. Drain and set aside.

Mash the potatoes with milk and salt. Brush a deep 9 inch pie dish with olive oil and press the potatoes in. Brush with remaining olive oil. Bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes or until lightly browned.
Arrange onions, broccoli and cheese in the potato crust. Whisk together the eggs, milk, salt, pepper and nutmeg. Pour over broccoli and cheese.
Bake in preheated oven for 30 to 40 minutes, until slightly puffed and cooked throughout. Allow to cool for 10 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Broccoli Quiche with Mashed Potato Crust
raw_recipe.description: A broccoli and cheese quiche in a light, crispy potato crust. A new twist on a familiar favorite. And a great way to use left over potatoes!

review.reviewBody: Delicious!!! I think the key to getting the potato crust to be more like a crust is to bake it on the bottom rack in your oven. A couple of minor changes I made was I used 4 eggs instead of 3, I am SURE I didn't use a full cup of milk (probably more like 1/2 cup), and no nutmeg. I used a little bit of garlic powder in the eggs along with the salt and pepper. It was SO good!! You could really change this up a lot with different cheeses and veggies. My 2.5 and 3.5 year olds LOVED this!! I was so surpised! And my choosy husband said I should definitely make this again. I think it's a keeper!!

This was good with these changes: I added fresh garlic to the potatoes while they were boiling. I used half & half instead of milk (in all cases). I added 2 Tbsp of grated parmesan cheese, black pepper and an egg to the mashed potato. I cooked the crust for 20 minutes on the bottom oven rack and then continued cooking in top of oven until lightly browned. I used sharp cheddar cheese and seasoned salt . I did NOT steam the broccoli first - this is not needed if you cut the broccoli in smaller pieces and use only the broccoli flower.
Fantastic. I made a cheez-it crust instead to add extra flavor, came out great! (put 2 cups of cheez-its, I used the white cheddar kind, in the food processor with 4 tablespoons of butter)

It is my go-to potato crust quiche. 
I used shredded potatoes with little oil and pepper as crust, baked it before adding the remaining ingredients. I added sweet peppers and super greens too. 

Very tasty, presents well!

I actually changed quite a bit, so I used this recipe as a base. For crust I sprinkled shredded cheddar on bottom of 10 inch glass pie dish. (The oils from cheese made it so it did not stick) I then mixed leftover mash potatoes from Thanksgiving with a some Italian bread crumbs & a teaspoon of flour (though I'm not sure if flour was needed). I then pressed the mixture on top of cheese to form crust and sprinkled again with crumbs. Baked for 15 minutes, then sprinkled more cheese on top. Baked another (maybe) 10 minutes which lead me to a nice crust to work with. (The cheese helped encase the potatoes to make a pretty solid crust that wasn't mushy like some comments have stated.) I then cooked zesty sausage in one pan, sauteed spinach, mushrooms, peppers, garlic, green onion etc. in another and transferred sausage and veggies to crust. Whisked 4 eggs w/ milk (I eyeball my recipes) and pepper, baked for 15 minutes then sprinkled just a bit more cheese on top (I love cheese) and baked 15 minutes more. I let it cool a bit, as the eggs are still cooking even out of the oven. It set up wonderful and my boyfriend really liked it. I know I changed a lot, but I only gave three stars because my first crust attempt like the recipe says didn't fair well. But without this recipe I wouldn't have known where to start.

Oh my goodness this is how I am going to make quiche from now on. I used leftover mashed potatoes and added one egg to the potato mixture as other reviews suggested. I still used the 3 eggs in the quiche mixture. Also, I used half and half instead of milk in the quiche mixture. I did not add nutmeg. I used what veggies I had on hand, which were onion and red bell pepper. This quiche turned out light and airy just like in the fancy restaurants. I might add baking soda next time to get it rise more. DELICIOUS!
Wonderful quick and east dish, made a couple of additions for my taste, added mushrooms to onions, added turmeric, garlic and chilli for extra tang, only a little of each so be careful with spices.

Had tons of left over mashed potato and cooked broccoli from a luncheon, this was a delicious way to use it up. I did add an egg to the mashed potato to help firm it up, only used 1/2c milk in the eggs and omitted the nutmeg. Yum!

Made almost as printed and it was very easy, quick and delicious. I cheated by using Idahoan instant potatoes (many flavor options, I used garlic). I used fresh broccoli steamed briefly in microwave. My husband ate all the leftovers- it reheats very well. Good as is but next time going to add bacon.

I'm going to make this tmrw, but 3 potatoes to mash. and 10-12 oz frozen broccoli the first time because I have it on hand. I don't see the point of precooking the broccoli and i will not do that, my fresh or froz broccoli will go into the oven as is . I won't be using a pie pan for mine. Can't wait to taste it. Thanks. And i love nutmeg. It tastes great in many types of foods. People complaining because they aren't fans of or familiar with uses of nutmeg. I will definitely put it into mine. Yum. I am sure it is good with and without the nutmeg. I like many of the other suggestions from the other people too--thanks, and will also tweak mine to my own tastes, can add other ingredients and so on. This is a good basic idea.

Was easy and tasty. I used canned milk. I increased to 2 cups of cheese and added in some chopped red pepper. I cut up some small potatoes I had on hand and boiled those. I used a large metal spatula to press into my quiche dish. The cheese baked into a nice brown crust on top. Next time I will add in more peppers and maybe some fresh mushroom.
I caramelized the onions separately and I think it added a lot of flavor. Other than that, I followed to the letter.
I mix it up this time I added some diced green pepper and red onion with an extra egg and extra cheese
I added a teaspoon of two of garam masala with the nutmeg, and we enjoyed that addition.
Too much salt
I made it today and loved it. I only used two cups of milk, though. Next time I will double the cheese and probably add some mushrooms. Thanks for sharing :)
This was OK. Some people may choose to add it to their repeat recipes, but I am giving it a pass. It was too bland for me.
